The website plots intelligence against cost to show the cheapest model achieving each score. However, this plot uses a logarithmic cost scale. It obscures massive price gaps between cheap and heavy models. It relies on official A P I. pricing instead of cheaper third party options like OpenRouter. It also displays local models at expensive datacenter rates. A revised analysis adjusts these factors as of September first, twenty twenty-six. It replaces logarithmic scales with a linear scale because human money is not logarithmic. It updates pricing for models including Kimi K three, Qwen three point eight Max, DeepSeek V four Flash zero seven thirty-one, G. L. M. dash five point three, G. L. M. dash five point three Dash Flash, and Hy three to reflect OpenRouter rates. It calculates local costs for sub-thirty-five-billion-parameter models based on electricity instead of datacenter fees. Local electricity costs use output tokens per task and local decode speeds on a used R. T. X. thirty ninety video card priced around fourteen hundred dollars. They use a US weighted average residential electricity price of zero point two zero four nine dollars per kilowatt-hour as of May twenty twenty-six. They add fifteen percent for uncached input tokens and tool calls while treating hardware cost as zero for dual-purpose machines. The comparison reveals steep diminishing returns in performance relative to cost. State-of-the-art models like, Fable five point one reach an intelligence score of sixty-six at three point six nine dollars per task. The G. L. M. dash five point three scores sixty at zero point four nine dollars per task. This makes it seven point five times cheaper. Descending further, the G. L. M. dash five point three Dash Flash at high settings achieves an intelligence score of fifty-five at zero point zero two three dollars per task. This is one hundred and sixty times cheaper than Fable. Meanwhile, Qwen three point eight dash twenty-seven B delivers an intelligence score of fifty-two at zero point zero one five dollars in electricity per task when run locally by an enthusiast gamer.

item.title: Try Google Pics: Easy Image Creation and Editing in Google Workspace
item.description: Google is rolling out a new image creation and editing tool called Google Pics. It is coming to all Google A. I. Pro and Ultra subscribers over the coming weeks. Most Workspace business customers will also get the tool. The system runs on the Nano Banana image generation and editing model. It works as a standalone product and inside Google Workspace apps. The integration starts with Slides, Docs, and Drive. Google Pics includes fine-tuned editing capabilities for precise control. Object segmentation lets users isolate and transform specific objects with text prompts. It does this without altering the rest of the image. Users can execute multiple edits at the same time. People can also modify or translate text directly inside images. This happens without disrupting the design or changing the font. The tool generates multiple options from a single prompt. It supports real-time collaboration for teams and friends. Users can share creations and edit the same image together. Google built the tool directly into existing Workspace applications. The company wants to eliminate the need for users to jump between applications. People will no longer need to copy and paste or switch tabs when creating visuals.

item.title: BGP Hijack Infecting Networks Caused By a Comedy of Errors That's Not Funny at All
item.description: Unknown hackers carried out a supply chain attack. They used B. G. P. hijacking to install malware. The target was Virtualizor. That is a management platform for virtualized environments. It was developed by Softaculous. The attackers exploited routing security weaknesses. They targeted hosting provider Hetzner Online. They also used flaws in the T. L. S. certificate issuance process. These actions seized control of I. P. addresses. The addresses belonged to Softaculous. Softaculous used the space for software updates. They also hosted a client and billing site there. The attackers pushed malicious software disguised as legitimate updates. The successful breach relied on two main failures. Hetzner Online had lax configuration of routing security. Softaculous failed to implement code signing to validate software updates. A thirty-three-hour window saw traffic intermittently misdirected. This happened across two spans. Hetzner reclaimed the address space twelve hours after the hijacking started. They did this by announcing the correct path. Then Hetzner stopped announcing it. This allowed the attacker to execute the same hijack a second time. It took Hetzner nearly ten hours to react during the second breach. Softaculous warned on Monday during the incident window. Any Virtualizor installation with diverted traffic could have received a malicious update package. The package came from the attacker server. Softaculous added that product update clients did not yet cryptographically verify update packages. A modified package would not have been rejected on that basis. The company believes only a small number of servers were actually affected. They cannot produce a definitive list. They advise treating every Virtualizor server as in scope for checks.

item.title: How we could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora
item.description: Cloudflare has built a new system called Cache Transcoding to expand effective cache capacity while memory costs go up. The architecture was built during the one point one point one point one Intern Program. It encodes eligible assets with the Zstandard lossless compression algorithm inside the Pingora proxy before writing them to disk. Initial testing over one million requests across ten cache servers showed strong results. The prototype shrunk eligible assets to one-third of their original on-disk size on average. The system uses zstd level three. It targets uncompressed compressible text responses such as H T M L., J S O N., C S S., and JavaScript. These files must have a known content length of at least four kibibytes. Media files like images, video, and fonts are excluded because they are typically compressed already. The architecture trades a small single-digit percentage increase in origin-facing C P U. usage for petabytes of effective cache capacity. It also reduces data transfer across data centers via Tiered Cache. The encoding cost is paid once upon cache entry. Storage and bandwidth savings recur every time the asset is reused. For next steps, Cloudflare plans to evaluate higher zstd levels. They will test a broader range of content types and object sizes. They want to tune different parameters from the eligibility criteria and examine range requests. They also plan to test pre-compressed origin responses and pass compressed objects directly to downstream components that support it.

item.title: Muse superapp from Meta and Ava model with computer use
item.description: Meta is preparing to launch a new agent super app named Muse. This aligns the product with the branding of the company's new generation of artificial intelligence models, known as A. I. models. The project was previously known internally as Project Hatch. The clearest change has appeared on iOS, where an internal testing app has transitioned into a Muse waitlist experience. Joining the waitlist appears technically possible, although Meta has not yet opened it publicly. Meta is also updating its desktop app with theme support and secondary color selection along with a monochrome theme. More significantly, Meta has added a setting for computer use. The company is testing a model variant called Ava. This variant is described as supporting computer control, although Ava itself is not currently accessible. These additions indicate that Muse could allow an A. I. agent to operate desktop applications and browse the web as part of longer, multi-step tasks. This places the product closer to tools like Codex and Claude. This direction mirrors the broader strategy at Meta. Versions one point one and one point two of Muse Spark already emphasize tool use, coding, and computer control. Previous reports regarding Project Hatch indicated the product would be capable of using websites and managing schedules. It would also handle sending emails and building custom tools. Meta was reportedly considering premium pricing as high as two hundred dollars per month. The transition to a waitlist suggests a controlled rollout. Meta could announce the app first and gradually admit users while computer and browser control features mature.

item.title: New Mexico’s largest reservoir plunges to just 1.4% full
item.description: New Mexico's largest reservoir, Elephant Butte Reservoir, plunged to just one point four percent capacity on July twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six. That reached its lowest level since nineteen seventy-one. According to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Earth Observatory, the severe decline was driven by years of extreme drought across the Rio Grande basin. It worsened in twenty twenty-six by the earliest snowmelt on record in the southern Rocky Mountains. The drop exposed long submerged debris and covered boat ramps with sediment at Elephant Butte Lake State Park. State officials reported that agricultural water releases concluded after July twenty-eighth. That allowed the reservoir to begin slowly rising again. The shrinking water supply underscores mounting pressure on Rio Grande resources relied upon by farms in New Mexico and Texas. Those farms produce crops including alfalfa, cotton, onions, pecans, and Hatch green chiles. To help managers navigate the limited supplies, initiatives backed by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Western Water Action Office are utilizing satellite measurements. They also use soil moisture data and drone observations to track water availability. These tools monitor groundwater pumping and support resource allocation along the valley.

item.title: Channel smuggling gangs resort to 'mega-dinghies' as crackdown limits small boat supply
item.description: People smuggling gangs on the northern shores of France are now using larger vessels. These mega dinghies are replacing small boats because of increased policing. A British Broadcasting Corporation investigation found that rival criminal groups are working together. They are loading more migrants onto fewer vessels. One fifteen meter boat recently carried a record two hundred thirty migrants toward the United Kingdom. French police claim they are intercepting two thirds of small boats before they reach the coast. This reduces crossing opportunities and drives up prices. Gangs are now quoting up to two thousand euros, or about seventeen hundred pounds, per person. Prices were about thirteen hundred euros a year ago. Payments are now required in cash to ensure commitment. The heightened police presence has also changed tactics. Gangs are launching operations in broad daylight using taxi boats arriving from as far away as Belgium. One observed small boat carried eighty two people into the shipping lane before reaching the United Kingdom successfully. Emergency teams on both sides of the Channel have raised concerns over the increased risk to life. On the fourth of August, one hundred seventy people had to be rescued after their vessel caught fire in the middle of the Channel. French officers claim they are intercepting two thirds of small boats while rioting police clear camps. The United Kingdom and France are announcing measures to increase the number of police officers on the French coast to try to stop the migrants.

item.title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
item.description: The world has entered a danger zone of extreme weather as a supersized El Niño develops. It could become the strongest in more than seventy years and last until at least February twenty twenty-seven. United Nations head, António Guterres warned that the planet is in uncharted waters. The natural weather phenomenon combines with human-induced climate change to boost global temperatures. Surface temperatures in the Pacific have been well over two degrees Celsius above average. Forecasts suggest monthly sea surface temperatures could get close to four degrees Celsius above average. This could make it the strongest El Niño since at least nineteen fifty by a large margin. Temperatures below the surface of the Pacific are even more exceptional. They are in places more than eight degrees Celsius above average. El Niño is changing global weather patterns. It brings drought to some regions and stronger typhoons and flooding to others. World Meteorological Organization Secretary-General, Celeste Saulo stated that the phenomenon has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies worldwide. Governments and scientists are taking measures to reduce risks. These include strengthened early warning systems and pre-emptive medical assistance. The impacts are already visible globally. In Panama, the number of vessels passing through the Panama Canal will be reduced by more than ten percent due to lower rainfall. This affects a waterway that sees about fourteen thousand ships per year and brings in about three billion dollars annually. In Indonesia, wildfires have burned more than one hundred seven thousand hectares. This prompted authorities to deploy cloud-seeding aircraft and arrest dozens over land-clearing allegations. Australia is bracing for severe marine heatwaves, particularly in the south. Meanwhile, China has experts linking effects of a super El Niño to expectations of typhoons making landfall. Peru faces risks of increased rainfall resulting in flash flooding and landslides. The United States announced the deployment of the vessel U. S. N. S. Comfort to the Peruvian coast with medical assistance and technical equipment.

item.title: September brings a dazzling Venus and a glowing Harvest Moon
item.description: September twenty twenty-six brings a busy lineup for skywatchers. N. A. S. A. point J. P. L. says Venus will look dazzling. The Harvest Moon will sit near Saturn and Neptune. The seasonal equinox and views of the Milky Way are also on the schedule. Between September fourteenth and twentieth, the Moon guides watchers toward Antares. That is a bright reddish star representing the heart of the constellation Scorpius. It also points to the Teapot star pattern in Sagittarius. Observers in dark locations may glimpse the hazy center of the Milky Way galaxy. It rises like steam from the Teapot spout. On September eighteenth, Venus reaches peak brilliance during its current evening appearance. It shines as an intensely bright point of light low in the west shortly after sunset. September nineteenth marks International Observe the Moon Night. This event encourages people worldwide to look at the Moon and learn about lunar science. On September twenty-second, the September equinox occurs. The Sun positions directly above Earth's equator. This marks the beginning of fall in the Northern Hemisphere and spring in the Southern Hemisphere. The month concludes on September twenty-sixth. The Harvest Moon rises in the eastern sky shortly after sunset. It sits near Saturn and the much fainter Neptune. Saturn is visible to the unaided eye. Neptune requires binoculars or a telescope at around magnitude eight.

item.title: Belkin introduces its first longer-lasting semi-solid-state power banks
item.description: Belkin is entering the semi-solid-state power bank market. The company joins brands like B. M. X., Kuxiu, and Zens by launching its first accessories with this battery technology. The new power banks use what Belkin calls BoostSolid Cell technology. This system adds a gel-like layer to the traditional liquid electrolyte found in standard lithium-ion batteries. Belkin says these accessories are engineered to last up to three times longer than other power banks. The technology also reduces the risk of overheating that could cause swelling or fires. Another advantage is consistent power delivery across a wider temperature range. These new devices offer durability and safety improvements. However, they cost more than comparable power banks with similar specifications.

item.title: Russia to close Goethe-Institut centres as Germany tensions escalate
item.description: Russia is closing German cultural centers across three cities. The affected locations are in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Yekaterinburg. This move comes in response to Germany shutting down a Russian cultural center in Berlin and a consulate in Bonn. The diplomatic escalation follows an incident on August fourth. An explosive-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig slash Halle airport and defused. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt accused Russia on Tuesday of being behind the hybrid attack. Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Germany on Tuesday of planting evidence in order to blame Moscow. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Wednesday that Germany deliberately took the step. He stated that this means the end of their cultural presence in Russia. The Goethe-Institut in Moscow originally opened in nineteen ninety-two. Following the airport incident, European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas described it as having the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism. European Union foreign ministers agreed to work on a proposal to impose sanctions on one thousand six hundred individuals and entities. These targets are linked to Russia's military industry for potential adoption next month.

item.title: NBA fines Clippers $30m, suspends several executives in Kawhi Leonard probe
item.description: The National Basketball Association has fined the Los Angeles Clippers thirty million dollars. The league took away five first-round draft picks from twenty twenty-nine to twenty thirty-three. Multiple top executives are suspended after a one-year independent investigation into salary cap rules involving star forward, Kawhi Leonard. The probe found a pattern of misconduct by the organization. The team introduced Leonard to club sponsors for off-court income and endorsement deals. They offered companies team business as inducements and paid personal expenses for Leonard and his representatives. The businesses involved included Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, Lockton Insurance, and Aspiration Partners. Aspiration Partners allegedly signed Leonard to a twenty-eight million dollar endorsement deal. That same company held a twenty-three-year, three-hundred-million-dollar sponsorship with the Clippers. Owner Steve Ballmer received a one-year suspension from all league and team activities. He tried to help Leonard obtain off-court income. He approved a business deal that was a precondition for Aspiration and failed to enforce league rules. Team president of business operations, Gillian Zucker, was suspended without pay for one year. Basketball operations president, Lawrence Frank, was suspended without pay for six months. They were involved in the arrangements and approved impermissible expenses. Zucker also provided false statements to investigators. Leonard is thirty-five years old and was personally fined seven hundred thousand dollars. His uncle and former business manager, Dennis Robertson, was banned from league business for five years for failing to report improper solicitations. The Clippers issued a statement. They vehemently reject the findings as the result of a biased investigation. They intend to vigorously challenge the penalties through arbitration. Leonard stated through his agent, Harrison Gaines, that he had no knowledge of any intent to circumvent the salary cap. He accepted responsibility for lapses in judgment by his inner circle. The penalties are final and binding under an agreement between the N. B. A. and the National Basketball Players Association. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations of collectively bargained compensation systems. Meanwhile, the Toronto Raptors had agreed in principle on June thirty to a trade to bring Leonard back. The league statement did not clarify whether he has been cleared to join the team.

item.title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies
item.description: A toxic haze is blanketing parts of Indonesia and spreading into Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines. Weeks of wildfires have been burning across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo since mid-July. The smog has exposed millions of people to pollution levels more than fifteen times the recommendation from the W. H. O. A super El Niño weather pattern is fueling these intense drought conditions. Between July and August, the Health Ministry in Indonesia recorded over fifty thousand respiratory infection cases linked to the fires. More than twelve thousand of these cases affected children under five years old. Malaysia has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis. Residents in the Philippine island province of Palawan reported mild headaches and itchy eyes, nose, and throat. The crisis is driven by both drought and human activity. This includes decades of land-use changes and drained peatlands along with industrial plantations. The fires are burning through one of the largest tropical peatland ecosystems in the world. When these areas are drained or burned, they can become carbon bombs, as warned by Doctor Nisa Novita, from Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara. Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo, from Institut Pertanian Bogor University, cited research warning about the scale of the disaster. This year's El Niño could burn an area as large as eleven million hectares. This is comparable to the severe wildfire season from nineteen ninety-seven to nineteen ninety-eight in Indonesia. The forestry minister in Indonesia, Raja Juli Antoni, stated earlier this week that the battle to extinguish the fires is entering a critical phase. He noted that September marks the peak of the El Niño conditions. Rizma Nur Fatimah, a nineteen-year-old teaching assistant in South Kalimantan, described the grim conditions. She said that inside her house with everything closed, the haze still got in. It became so thick that you could not see your own feet.

item.title: The Download: rethinking child safety and fossil-fueled farming
item.description: New York City has implemented a one-year ban on generative A. I. in elementary and middle schools. The ban affects six hundred thousand students. The moratorium applies to any software utilizing student-facing generative A. I. In other technology news, Uber launched the United Kingdom's first commercial robotaxi service. The service utilizes technology from the startup Wayve. A United States judge rejected the government's demand to force a sale of Google's ad tech business. The ruling allows the company to avoid a breakup. Google still faces requirements to change how it treats rivals and shares information. Nikhil Lai stated that courts remain hesitant to dismantle complex tech systems even when finding anticompetitive conduct. In Taiwan, authorities have uncovered a hidden Chinese network. The network is linked to one hundred sixty-six cases of illegal operations and talent poaching targeting the island's chip sector. The Trump administration has backed OpenAI in its copyright lawsuit brought by the New York Times. The Justice Department argued that A. I. training can constitute fair use. The department added that national security depended on United States tech dominance.

item.title: NASA scientists discover a giant 10-sided pattern on Saturn
item.description: Scientists have discovered a giant ten sided atmospheric pattern circling Saturn's south pole. This gives the planet a surprising counterpart to its famous northern hexagon. The findings were published in Science Advances on September third, twenty twenty-six. The research reveals that the strange decagon is a vertically extended structure embedded inside a powerful jet stream. Researchers reconstructed the development of the feature using Hubble Space Telescope observations dating back to twenty twenty-three. They also used ground-based images from twenty twenty-four and twenty twenty-five. These images were submitted by amateur astronomers Trevor Barry and Jean-Paul Oger to the Planetary Virtual Observatory Laboratory. Study lead author, Agustín Sánchez-Lavega, from the University of the Basque Country helped confirm the findings. Data from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration spacecraft, known as Cassini, showed that no similar formation existed in the south between two thousand four and two thousand seventeen. Saturn's seasonal cycle made the south pole visible from Earth recently. The wave gradually strengthened from faint initial signs into a clear decagon. Amy Simon, a study co-author, noted the rarity of the event. She directs the Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy program at the Goddard Space Flight Center. She stated that the northern hexagon has been present for over forty years. This new feature is different because it appears to be strengthening. Researchers now have the opportunity to watch a giant atmospheric pattern develop. Scientists do not yet know what triggered the decagon. They are also unsure whether it will persist like its northern counterpart. Continued observations will use the Hubble telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope. Computer modeling will also help determine its survival. These tools will reveal more about atmospheric dynamics on giant planets.

item.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence ‘whatsoever’ Morocco behind Ceuta border breach
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, told parliament that Spain has seen no evidence that Morocco planned the border breach in Ceuta. This followed a police report claiming Moroccan border forces actively aided about seventy thousand people to cross in late July. Sánchez stated that no institution, including the European Commission, has provided solid evidence of Moroccan involvement. He conceded that Moroccan forces allowed crossings during a ten hour period on the thirtieth of July. Moroccan officials have denied enabling the crossing. Sánchez also denied receiving any warning ahead of the influx. About fifty thousand people marched in Madrid on Wednesday to protest the handling of the crisis. As many as one hundred forty-one people are thought to have died trying to enter Ceuta during the event. The event triggered a political and humanitarian crisis. On August twenty-first, Spain summoned the ambassador from Morocco over unacceptable statements by two ministers regarding Ceuta and Melilla. This included sovereignty claims by Moroccan justice minister, Abdellatif Ouahbi. Sánchez appealed for European solidarity. He noted that ninety percent of crossers returned within twenty-four hours. Several thousand remain, including at least five hundred minors. Amid calls from the party Vox to return them, Sánchez reminded members of parliament that migrants have a right to individual treatment under the law. He stated you cannot just grab someone by the arm and drag them across the frontier as though they were a sack of dirt. Sánchez concluded by noting the economic disparity between Ceuta and Morocco. He stated that even if they build a wall one hundred metres high, people would still be prepared to throw themselves into the sea to get across.

item.title: NeoMME: an efficient Multimodal-native and Multilingual Encoder
item.description: NeoMME is a family of two hundred sixty million and eight hundred million multilingual multimodal encoders. They process text tokens and raw image patches through a single bidirectional Transformer. They do not rely on a separate pretrained vision tower or a causal language model. They were trained from scratch using a masked discrete-diffusion objective on about five hundred twenty-four billion packed input tokens. The models feature a sixteen thousand three hundred eighty-four token context length and dynamic image resolution. When fine-tuned for visual document retrieval using the page-image approach, they are called NeoMME-Retriever. The models generate dense and late-interaction embeddings in one forward pass, bypassing optical character recognition preprocessing steps. Running on an NVIDIA L40S G P U. with a matched twenty forty-eight by twenty forty-eight image input size, the two hundred sixty million model encodes about fifty-one pages per second. This achieves roughly twice the throughput of ColModernVBERT. Hierarchical token pooling and asymmetric quantization reduce late-interaction index storage to six kilobytes per page. This is two hundred fifty-five times smaller while retaining more than ninety-five percent of baseline normalized discounted cumulative gain at ten. On the ViDoRe v3 benchmark, NeoMME-Retriever-Two-Hundred-Sixty-Million reaches zero point five two three for normalized discounted cumulative gain at ten. This is the highest score among evaluated models strictly below eight hundred million parameters. Meanwhile, the eight hundred million model reaches zero point five five six. Omar Khattab, who introduced late-interaction in ColBERT, explains why the term is more precise than multi-vector. It describes the granularity and learnability of the scoring function, not simply the number of stored vectors. Model checkpoints are available in Hugging Face Transformers under the Apache two point zero license.

item.title: Daybreak for Frontline Defenders: $1B to protect essential services
item.description: OpenAI is launching a one billion dollar global initiative called Daybreak for Frontline Defenders. It will provide subsidized access to frontier A. I. cyber capabilities and training. The funding is targeted for consumption over the next six months. It focuses on resource constrained operators of essential services. These include water and wastewater systems and electric grid operators. State and local governments and community and regional banks are also included. Nonprofits and open-source maintainers are part of the effort. The program includes Daybreak for America. This features a new pilot with the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center. The pilot will train and support state and local cyber defenders. Partners in the Daybreak Defense Network are announcing more than thirty-five products and services. These bring the models directly into the enterprise. The initiative builds on previous support. That earlier effort offered up to one million dollars in no-cost A. P. I. credits. It also provided technical assistance to water systems following recent attacks. OpenAI states that A. I. enabled cyber attacks will become more widespread and sophisticated in the coming months. This creates a narrowing defender window to close security gaps before attackers exploit them. Eligible organizations can visit the Daybreak website to learn more about access and support.

item.title: 7.8% growth, but a Rs 6 lakh crore question: Why GDP data has sparked a debate
item.description: India's G. D. P. growth for the first quarter beat estimates at seven point eight percent. The figure has sparked a heated debate over calculation methodologies and downward revisions of previous quarters. Former finance secretary, Subhash Chandra Garg questioned the data. He argued that without downward revisions, nominal growth would be about two point six percent with real growth near zero. In February, the government shifted the G. D. P. base year from twenty eleven to twenty twelve, moving to twenty twenty-two to twenty twenty-three. This revised the first quarter fiscal twenty-six baseline from eighty-six point zero five lakh crore rupees down to eighty lakh crore rupees. The government maintains that old and new series figures cannot be directly compared. The revisions incorporate improved methodologies, updated data sources, and the recent Household Consumption Expenditure Survey of twenty twenty-two to twenty twenty-three. Soumya Kanti Ghosh, member of the sixteenth Finance Commission and group chief economic adviser at S. B. I., criticized critics who mix old and new series numbers. He stated this is completely unsolicited and a sure sign of intellectual dishonesty. Ghosh calculated that comparing the new first quarter fiscal twenty-seven nominal G. D. P. of eighty-eight point three lakh crore rupees against the updated base yields a nine point seven percent growth rate. This translates to a real growth of seven point four percent. Economists also addressed a puzzle surrounding the two point five percent implied G. D. P. deflator. It sits below the C. P. I. inflation rate of three point nine percent. Experts like, D. K. Srivastava of E. Y. India noted that the new series uses a double deflation method for selected sectors. This separates output and intermediate goods price adjustments. The methodology caused manufacturing nominal G. V. A. to grow seven point seven percent while real G. V. A. grew nine point two percent. This resulted in a negative implicit G. V. A. deflator because input prices rose faster than output prices amid the Middle East conflict and companies absorbed higher costs. Economists note that quarterly G. D. P. revisions are a periodic exercise. Ghosh points out that the latest first quarter fiscal twenty-seven number will get finalized by February twenty twenty-nine only. This means we have to wait for thirty months to finally know where the numbers stand.

item.title: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
item.description: Artificial intelligence is changing mathematics quickly. This was the main topic on a live episode of The Joy of Why. The show was recorded on July twenty-sixth, twenty twenty-six, at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia. Hosts Janna Levin and Steven Strogatz spoke with three experts. The guests were Akshay Venkatesh from the Institute for Advanced Study, Ravi Vakil from Stanford University, and Alex Kontorovich from Rutgers University. The panel discussed major recent milestones. Google’s AlphaProof won a silver medal at the twenty twenty-four International Mathematical Olympiads. Then a DeepThink model secured a gold medal in twenty twenty-five. Other recent A. I. solutions targeted problems in Tom Bloom’s database of Erdős problems. Kontorovich highlighted one specific breakthrough. An A. I. model autonomously built a counterexample that disproved the conjectured value of the Erdős unit distance conjecture. This solution inspired human mathematicians to solve an unrelated sum product problem using techniques exposed by the A. I. The panel also addressed challenges from machine-generated mathematics. Venkatesh and Vakil raised concerns about low-quality submissions. The flood of A. I. generated proofs threatens to overwhelm mathematical journals and strain community peer review systems. Vakil noted that mathematicians will face a massive influx of material. He joked about checking his inbox after the event and dreading the kind of A. I. slop people will send him. The discussion highlighted a broader philosophical shift in the field. Mathematicians are now grappling with a fundamental question. They wonder if the true value of mathematics lies strictly in the final destination of a solved theorem or in the human journey of discovery and learning.

item.title: .name Termination
item.description: Fraser registered neil dot fraser dot name long ago for his website and his email and an application programming interface server. He later registered beverly dot fraser dot name following his daughter's birth. On April fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, Verisign proposed destroying the entire third level of the name hierarchy to simplify administration. The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers approved this action on July twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six. Fraser learned of it when his registrar emailed him a few days prior to his announcement. Fraser originally chose the domain because Global Name Registry operated it rather than Verisign. Verisign later acquired Global Name Registry and included numerous lies in its proposal. The upcoming termination means Fraser's website and his email address and his connected Internet of Things devices will vanish in February. This happens even though his domain is paid for until twenty forty. Once the third-level domains are terminated, vacant second-level domains are assumed to become available for registration. This allows someone else to scoop up fraser dot name and recreate neil dot fraser dot name. They can hijack hundreds of accounts and commit code and seize control of his devices. Fraser notes he is just one of twenty-two thousand people who will lose their domains in this change. He concludes that it is time to lawyer up.

item.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
item.description: Google DeepMind and Google Research have introduced WeatherNext three. It is a global weather A. I. model that generates hourly forecasts at higher resolutions and improved accuracy. Independent live evaluations by Brightband show it is the most advanced and accurate global weather model to date. WeatherNext three trains directly on real-time observations and sparse weather station data. This avoids lagging physics simulations. The model produces surface variables like temperature and moisture at a five-kilometer resolution. Other surface variables appear at ten kilometers. Atmospheric variables like wind speed appear at twenty-five kilometers. This provides a global weather picture roughly five times sharper than its predecessor. That predecessor was WeatherNext two, which used a twenty-five-kilometer grid in six-hour increments. This setup enables the model to update hourly and bypass traditional modeling constraints. For precipitation forecasting, the model shows a Continuous Ranked Probability Score improvement of up to sixty percent against N. A. S. A. dot IMERG. It improves by thirty percent for M. R. M. S. It improves by ten percent against rain gauge measurements for early lead times. The model also features predictions engineered for renewable energy production. These include one-hundred-meter wind speeds for wind-energy output. They also include high-resolution cloud cover and sun radiation levels for solar farms. Starting today, WeatherNext three is powering weather experiences across Google Search. It is also in the Gemini app, Google Maps, the Google Maps Platform Weather A P I., and Google Earth Engine. When planning a day or more ahead, people will see up to fifty percent more accurate precipitation forecasts. The greatest improvements happen in regions where forecasts have historically been less reliable. The forecast data is also available to query in BigQuery and Earth Engine. Users can also access bulk downloads from Google Cloud Storage.

item.title: OpenAI Cut Off a Billion-Dollar Customer to Avoid Elon Musk
item.description: OpenA. I. is ending its partnership with the coding startup Cursor. The relationship was projected to bring in more than one billion dollars in annualized revenue by the spring of twenty twenty-six. Cursor was one of the top five customers for OpenA. I. at the start of twenty twenty-six. They paid fees to offer OpenA. I. models to developers. This decision follows a massive acquisition. SpaceX bought Cursor in a sixty billion dollar deal. The move helps OpenA. I. show investors a stable business as the company prepares to go public next year. OpenA. I. stated they cannot trust Elon Musk. They cited past experiences with his companies violating contracts. The blog post explained they cannot be confident that SpaceX will use their technology within the terms of service. OpenA. I. also noted an incident from earlier this year. Musk apparently admitted during a deposition that x. A. I. used OpenA. I. models to train its own models. That business is now part of SpaceX. Cursor leader, Michael Truell, responded to the news. He claimed that OpenA. I. models serve only about five percent of Cursor user traffic. OpenA. I. executive, Thibault Sottiaux, quickly pushed back. He stated that token usage is not a proxy for revenue or value created. He asked the leader to share the math. Meanwhile, Anthropic cofounder, Tom Brown, made an announcement. He stated that Anthropic will continue making Claude models available in Cursor.

item.title: NASA to Cover Progress 96 Spacecraft Launch, Docking
item.description: National Aeronautics and Space Administration will provide live coverage of the launch and docking of the unpiloted Roscosmos Progress ninety-six cargo spacecraft. The spacecraft carries about three tons of food, fuel, and supplies for the crew aboard the International Space Station. The resupply spacecraft is scheduled to launch on a Soyuz rocket at twelve-fifteen p.m., or nine-fifteen p.m. Baikonur time, on Wednesday, September ninth. The launch happens from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. National Aeronautics and Space Administration live launch coverage begins at twelve p.m. After a two-day trip to the space station, the Progress spacecraft will dock autonomously to the Poisk module space-facing port. That docking happens at two-thirty-seven p.m. on Friday, September eleventh. National Aeronautics and Space Administration arrival coverage begins at one-forty-five p.m. The spacecraft will remain docked for about five months. Then it will depart to re-enter Earth atmosphere. It will harmlessly burn up over the Pacific Ocean. Before the Progress ninety-six spacecraft arrives, an older spacecraft will leave. The Progress ninety-four spacecraft will undock from the space station at approximately eleven-eighty-one a.m., wait, eleven-eighteen a.m., on Monday, September seventh. That is for its departure and planned destructive re-entry. National Aeronautics and Space Administration will not stream coverage of that undocking.

item.title: Psilocybin could prevent common and debilitating chemotherapy side effect
item.description: Psilocybin may prevent nerve damage caused by chemotherapy drugs. About seventy-five percent of cancer patients face this debilitating side effect. Chemotherapy drugs disrupt the transport of energy to nerve endings. The nerve endings wear out and retract as a result. Tests on nerve samples from mice and humans showed promising results. Psilocybin maintained the energy supply and caused less nerve damage. Mice with abdominal tumours received two injections of psilocybin. Each dose was equivalent to twenty-five milligrams in humans. The injections were spaced one week apart. The mice then received daily injections of the chemotherapy drug cisplatin for one week. Pain-sensitivity tests revealed important findings. Mice receiving psilocybin before cisplatin responded normally compared to a control group. Mice receiving cisplatin without psilocybin showed heightened sensitivity to pain. Researchers warn patients not to take psilocybin at home. The drug is not proven safe or effective during chemotherapy. It can also interact dangerously with cancer medications. A randomised controlled trial will begin in November. The study involves about eighty people with various types of cancer. Results are expected in about five years. Moran Amit at M. D. Anderson noted that no drug previously prevented this condition. Effective treatments currently lack beyond moderate pain relief from duloxetine. Maria Maiaru at the University of Reading spoke about the research. She was not involved in the study itself. She stated that successful clinical trials could help patients avoid chronic pain. Patients might also require fewer chemotherapy dose reductions and interruptions.

item.title: Vance says Fed should lower interest rates: 'Would be nice to have some help'
item.description: Vice President J. D. Vance said Thursday that the Federal Reserve should cut interest rates to help make homes more affordable. This adds to pressure from President Donald Trump on the central bank to lower borrowing costs. Vance said his administration is trying to keep interest rates down and would appreciate help from the Federal Reserve. These remarks follow comments made less than a week earlier in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, by Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh. Warsh hinted at potentially hiking rates to address persistently high inflation and bring it down to the central bank target of two percent. Vance made his statements less than two weeks before the Federal Open Market Committee is set to convene. The committee will decide whether or not to adjust rates. Traders are currently about evenly split on the odds of a rate hike at the meeting scheduled for September fifteen to sixteen, according to data from the C. M. E. Group FedWatch gauge. On Tuesday, Fed Governor Michael Barr stated he would be prepared to back a rate increase if inflation stays elevated. Meanwhile, Governor Christopher Waller indicated Thursday morning that he is more likely to keep rates steady. The comments from Vance may add to concerns regarding the independence of the Federal Reserve under the Trump administration. The administration has aggressively pushed to slash rates and is trying to fire Governor Lisa Cook.

item.title: US senator calls on the NSA to give guidance for use of VPNs
item.description: A prominent United States senator is asking the National Security Agency to provide public guidance on best practices for using virtual private networks. These tools secure communications against foreign espionage. United States agencies have previously recommended virtual private networks. They route internet traffic through encrypted connections to remote servers and mask user internet protocol addresses. However, none have issued recommendations on which services offer adequate protection. A host of limitations can undo many expected protections. Encrypted tunnels often terminate once a single server decrypts traffic and sends it on to its final destination. This makes decrypted traffic or internet protocol addresses available for snooping by rogue employees or attackers. Furthermore, virtual private networks fail to encrypt certain metadata like time stamps. This allows nation-states to build profiles for intelligence gathering.

item.title: Trump claims US has ‘virtually unlimited’ ammunition for Iran war, slams ‘treasonous’ critics
item.description: President Donald Trump rejected reports that the United States is running short of ammunition in Iran. He called claims of dwindling supplies one hundred percent wrong. He labeled critics spreading those claims as treasonous. President Trump posted on Truth Social. He stated that the country has virtually unlimited amounts of mid- to high-grade ammunition. He said the nation is producing munitions at levels never seen before. This production builds up stockpiles for future contingencies. The United States temporarily prioritized keeping ammunition for domestic needs. Foreign sales will resume soon. President Trump criticized the previous Biden administration. He said they provided hundreds of billions of dollars in assistance to Ukraine and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization without requiring European allies to pay for it. His comments responded to recent news reports. An August fourth Reuters story cited three people familiar with the data. The story indicated that the United States Army has used virtually all of two key surface-to-surface missile systems during its five-month war. The first system is the Army Tactical Missile System. The second system is the newer Precision Strike Missile. The depletion of these long-range missiles has raised concerns among United States officials. Each missile costs more than one million dollars. Officials worry about Pentagon readiness for potential future conflicts with major adversaries like Russia and China. Military leaders warned the president in recent weeks that supplies of defensive weapons were falling. This includes Patriot missile interceptors. A United States official disputed claims that stockpile concerns stopped a major offensive. The official said pressure from Gulf states influenced the decision instead. A source familiar with the situation noted Central Command faced challenges. The source added they have been able to draw from global military stockpiles to replenish supplies.

item.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to lift block on USPS plan to restrict mail voting
item.description: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to lift a block on a US Postal Service plan. The plan aims to restrict mail-in voting for the midterm elections. Key parts of the plan are currently frozen by a temporary restraining order. A federal judge in Boston issued that order. The plan stems from a March executive order by President Trump. It would require state election officials to provide lists of mail-in voters names and addresses to the Postal Service. It would also require specific barcodes on ballot envelopes. Voting by mail remains available to all eligible voters for now. The U. S. P. S. is expected to deliver ballots as usual while the legal battle continues. However, many election experts warn it is too late to implement the plan without causing major disruptions. A whistleblower report claims the agency has not properly tested the online portal system meant to collect voter information. The report adds the agency has established a verification policy that could prevent many voters from receiving their ballots on time. Trump stated he issued the directives to prevent illegal voting by non-US citizens. Studies and audits indicate that issue is extremely rare. Challengers argue the plan is illegal because the postal agency lacks the authority to control mail-in voting. The Supreme Court previously ruled on a procedural question regarding one of the lawsuits in August. The justices have not yet ruled on the legality of the underlying order or the U. S. P. S. plan. North Carolina is scheduled to begin mailing absentee ballots on Friday. That officially launches the voting season for the midterms. Many other states are following later this month.

item.title: ICE agent charged with lying under oath about Minnesota shooting
item.description: Federal prosecutors have charged an immigration officer with lying under oath. The officer is, Christian Castro. The charges involve the shooting of a twenty-four-year-old man named, Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis. The shooting happened in January during an immigration crackdown in Minnesota. This case marks a rare prosecution by the Justice Department during a major enforcement campaign. Prosecutors allege that, Christian Castro, lied about the events leading up to the shooting. He fired through the door of a Minnesota home and hit the victim in the leg., Christian Castro, is a former Department of Homeland Security agent. He also faces multiple state felony charges in Minnesota related to the nonfatal shooting. Those charges include assault with a dangerous weapon. Minnesota authorities tried to extradite the officer from Texas. Texas Governor Greg Abbott declined to cooperate with the extradition request. That refusal led to the officer being detained in Texas for ninety days before his release under state law. The federal indictment followed the release of surveillance video. That video contradicted the officer's account that the victim had attacked him. Todd Lyons was the acting head of Immigration and Customs Enforcement at the time. He stated that the footage revealed sworn testimony from separate officers appeared to contain untruthful statements. The incident started after the officer and a fellow agent chased a Venezuelan national named, Alfredo Aljorna. The chase followed a traffic stop and ended at a home shared with the victim. The officer shot through the closed door. He knew the home was occupied by several people. A witness stated that two children were also inside the home. Federal authorities have suspended the officer and dropped initial charges against the victim and his co-defendant. The other agent involved in the chase has also been suspended but has not yet been charged.

item.title: Startup ARR is less secure than ever, new research shows
item.description: Seventy-four percent of one hundred fifty enterprise information technology professionals surveyed by venture capital firm Madrona plan to expand their artificial intelligence budgets over the next twelve months. The rest of the surveyed professionals plan to hold their spending steady. Fewer than half of enterprise artificial intelligence pilots ever reach full production. Seventy-seven percent of enterprises re-evaluate their artificial intelligence vendors every six months or on a rolling basis. Market researcher I. D. C. predicts companies will spend four point two five trillion dollars on technology in twenty twenty-six. That spending will be driven almost entirely by artificial intelligence. Madrona states in its report that this creates a fast in and fast out dynamic. This dynamic differs fundamentally from traditional enterprise software as a service. Traditional multi-year contracts used to provide a moat of inertia. Switching costs are lower in enterprise artificial intelligence and the re-evaluation cadence is relentless. This frequent reassessment leaves startup annual recurring revenue insecure even after products graduate from the pilot phase. More than half of technical artificial intelligence buyers want fees tied to work produced or outcomes. According to a. one. six. z. partners Tugce Erten, and Sarah Wang, pricing around recognizable work makes the product economically valuable to both sides. Enterprises remain willing to try new technology, but long-term revenue security from standard enterprise contracts has disappeared.

item.title: Home Secretary reviews Himalayan States’ preparedness for glacial lake outbursts
item.description: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan chaired a high-level meeting on Thursday, September third, twenty twenty-six. He met with Himalayan states and union territories to review preparedness for glacial lake outburst floods and snow avalanches. This review follows deadly flash floods in Nepal that killed hundreds and left thousands missing. Chief Secretaries and State Disaster Management Authorities attended from Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir. Senior officials also attended from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the National Disaster Management Authority. Representatives from the Central Water Commission and the India Meteorological Department joined them. Officials from the Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment were present as well. Officials reviewed the evolving threat of glacial lake outburst floods. They focused on vulnerable glacial lakes, high-risk zones, flow path mapping, and alert dissemination. Mister Mohan stressed that preparedness must move beyond a response-oriented approach. He said it must focus on preventive mitigation, risk reduction, and community-level readiness. The Centre directed states to expedite mitigation projects sanctioned in twenty twenty-four. States must strengthen inter-agency coordination. They must ensure continuous surveillance and regular sharing of risk information to minimize potential loss of life and property.

item.title: The Apple Vision Pro was used for a successful hip surgery
item.description: Medical technology company Stryker announced that its SportSuite Vision software for the Apple Vision Pro was used in a hip arthroscopy at Duke Health. This marks the first time the software has been utilized in a real world practice. Stryker says its SportSuite Vision software for the headset received De Novo authorization from the Food and Drug Administration in July. In the case of this inaugural operation, the mixed reality experience gave the surgeon access to Stryker planning tools, arthroscopic images, and computed tomography imaging while performing the procedure. Orthopedic surgeon, Doctor Chad Mather III, conducted the surgery using the device at Duke Health. He said that using spatial computing enabled him to customize the placement of key clinical information. It helped fit his workflow and access it within the sterile field. This helped create a more comfortable and streamlined operating room setup while keeping the information he needed in view.

item.title: Predictive tools can confuse rare mutations with dangerous ones
item.description: Most computer software used to predict dangerous D. N. A. mutations can confuse rare mutations with harmful ones. A new study in the American Journal of Human Genetics reveals this major flaw. A research team led by, Doctor Donate Weghorn at the Center for Genomic Regulation in Barcelona tested fifty prediction tools. They used thirteen point five million mutations spread across six thousand six hundred fifty-nine human genes. The tested programs included AlphaMissense built by Google DeepMind. They also tested E. V. E. and popE. V. E. co-developed by other research groups at the Center for Genomic Regulation. The study found that almost all the programs make critical errors. They overestimate the potential harm of mutations that are less likely to occur than average. They also underestimate the effect of more likely mutations. This happens because the software makes a faulty assumption. It assumes that D. N. A. spots remaining unchanged over millions of years always matter. It assumes changing them is harmful. The software fails to account for regional differences in how mutation-prone the genome is. For instance, the starting points of genes are thirty-five percent more prone to mutations than other regions. The researchers found that mutations in genes for D. N. A. repair, cilia, and sperm function are likely being overcalled as dangerous. Meanwhile, genes linked to intellectual disability and single-parent conditions are likely being undercalled. As, Doctor Weghorn stated, both outcomes would be bad. To test the tools, the team used experimental data from the laboratory of, Ben Lehner. Researchers there physically made hundreds of thousands of mutations across five hundred human protein fragments and measured the damage. The authors of the study state that a practical fix is possible. It would involve modifying the computer software to include information from maps. These maps show where the human genome is more or less mutation-prone.

item.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare
item.description: Terminal one at Berlin Brandenburg Airport reopened on Thursday evening. Federal police had evacuated the building at around five forty-five p.m. following a security scare. An unidentified woman reportedly told security staff at a service point that she had a dangerous substance in her luggage. A police spokesperson told the dpa news agency that a potential threat from the substance could not be ruled out. Police gave the all-clear at around eight forty-five p.m. They confirmed that nobody had been in danger at any point. Analysis results for the substance are expected in the coming days. An airport spokeswoman stated that the police operation had ended. Despite the reopening, operations remained restricted on Thursday evening. Delays and some cancellations were expected until the end of the day. Flights were not stopped entirely. Incoming arrivals and prepared departures continued. Passenger processing was partially relocated to Terminal two. An airport press officer told D. W. that around thirty flights had been delayed. The incident also temporarily disrupted the city S-Bahn train service and Deutsche Bahn regional trains. Regular operations are scheduled to resume on Friday.
